# Architecture

## Project Type

CLI + TUI tool using a simple, flat architecture: `main.go` wires cobra commands; `internal/cli` holds subcommands, `internal/tui` the bubbletea app (app/models/screens/components), `internal/mcp` the go-sdk service layer and transports. Distributed as cross-platform release binaries and the `@standardbeagle/mcp-tui` npm wrapper.

No active migrations. Document ongoing migrations here.

## Project Constraints

- Desktop distribution: GitHub Releases binaries (linux/darwin/windows) + npm wrapper (`bin/`, `scripts/install.js`). Runs locally; no hosted service.
- SSE transport connects with `context.Background()`, never the CLI timeout context — the timeout kills the hanging GET.
- Every stdio command passes `config.ValidateCommand` before exec.
- Child-process tests spawn PowerShell 7 (`pwsh`); CI sets `MCP_TUI_REQUIRE_PWSH=1` so a missing pwsh fails instead of skipping.
- No MCP servers are configured directly in this repo (`.mcp.json`, settings). Agent MCP access goes through slop-mcp.

## Exposure Posture

| Listener | Code | Posture | Caps |
|---|---|---|---|
| OAuth auth-code callback | `internal/mcp/oauth/local_server.go` | `loopback` (`127.0.0.1`, ephemeral port, one request) | `ReadHeaderTimeout` 10s only |

Known gaps (not yet fixed):
- `--oauth-redirect-host` help text says "loopback only", but the host is passed to `net.Listen` unvalidated — `0.0.0.0` binds every interface.
- No max connections, `MaxHeaderBytes`, `ReadTimeout`, or `WriteTimeout` on the callback server.
- `resultCh` is buffered 1; a second callback request blocks its handler on send, so `srv.Shutdown(context.Background())` can hang.

## Side Effect Isolation

All side effects (I/O, network, database, filesystem) must be isolated at system boundaries:

- Pure business logic must not depend on external services directly
- Side-effectful operations are pushed to the edges of the system
- Use dependency injection or explicit parameter passing to provide external dependencies
- Test pure logic without mocks; mock only at system boundaries

## Configuration Format Preferences

- Use **KDL** for application configuration (settings, keybindings, preferences)
- Use **JSON** for content data, API contracts, and LLM-consumed formats
- Use environment variables for deployment-specific secrets and connection strings
